property.claim: On the configured SMP x86-64 profile, starting from zero and in the absence of any other update, two completed concurrent executions of the failed_load_modules atomic_inc() contribute exactly two; the final value one is impossible.
property.concurrency_argument: The pinned source documents module-load races and exposes init_module/finit_module entry points; mod_stat_bump_invalid() is reached after per-list module_mutex critical sections, and failed_load_modules is a kernel-wide incremental statistic.
exclusions: The claim assumes initial value zero, exactly two selected increments, and no concurrent third update; it is a no-lost-update property, not a claim about an arbitrary debugfs snapshot.
The model omits invalid_mod_bytes, allocation, error-path functionality, module lifetime, and whole module-loader behavior.
The no-return atomic_inc operation is relaxed with respect to other locations; no cross-object ordering is claimed.
Counter wraparound is defined by the kernel contract but excluded from this two-increment zero-origin property.
No architecture implementation other than the configured SMP x86-64 profile is accepted by this source-linked pilot.
No progress, fairness, lock-freedom, wait-freedom, runtime reachability frequency, or whole-kernel race-freedom property is claimed.
property.implementation_argument: The kernel atomic_t contract makes RMW operations SMP atomic; the pinned LKMM model treats atomic_inc as one RMW, and the configured x86-64 object lowers the selected increment to lock incl against the counter's local .bss location.
property.lifetime_argument: failed_load_modules is a translation-unit-local static atomic_t with zero initialization and no reset, decrement, alternative write, or deallocation in the pinned translation unit.
